title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the previous page's attempt to recast an 'atelier spatial', a structure (A, ⊴, |o|) with a symmetric relation |o| ('disjonction'/orthogonality). Grothendieck now takes the set Σ = Σ_A as the base set.

He defines a 'spatiale (ensembliste)' as a triple (Σ, ≤, C) with three axioms:
- Spat 1: ≤ is an order with least element 0_Σ and greatest element 1_Σ, and with arbitrary sups. Hence it also has arbitrary infs, so (Σ, ≤) is a complete lattice.
- Spat 2: C² = id and x ≤ y ⇔ Cy ≤ Cx. So C is an involutive order anti-automorphism.
- Spat 3: x ∧ Cx = 0_Σ, equivalently x ∨ Cx = 1_Σ.

In modern terms this is exactly a complete ortholattice (complete orthocomplemented lattice; no distributivity or orthomodularity is assumed).

He then defines orthogonality by X |o| Y ⇔ X ≤ CY ⇔ Y ≤ CX, and derives:
- X |o| Y ⇒ X ∧ Y = 0;
- |o| is symmetric;
- X |o| X ⇔ X = 0.
So on Σ* = Σ∖{0}, |o| is symmetric and irreflexive: an orthogonality space in the sense of Dacey / Foulis–Randall.

The 'Ex' paragraph begins the converse construction. Start from any set A with a symmetric relation |o|. A model case is A a set of regions of a space with |o| = 'interior disjointness'; there A_0 = ∅.
- A_0 is first defined as {X : X |o| X}. It is then corrected to {X : X |o| Y for all Y}, which the next page calls A_00.
- The 'rapports' are the biorthogonally closed subsets of A. They form Σ ⊂ P(A), stable under arbitrary intersections, so a complete lattice. The orthogonal map gives C with C² = id.
- The condition x ∧ Cx = 0 holds iff X |o| X ⇒ X ∈ A_00 (shown on the next page).

The next page also checks that starting from (Σ, |o|_Σ) the closure construction gives back Σ, via orth(A) = C(Sup A). This is the standard duality between orthogonality spaces and complete ortholattices, i.e. Birkhoff's polarity/Galois-connection construction.

The purpose is to axiomatize 'spatial ateliers', an abstract set-theoretic notion of space built from regions and their disjointness, by an intrinsic lattice-with-involution structure.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. 'Sup quelconques (donc aussi Sup' quelconques)' correctly means that arbitrary sups imply arbitrary infs in a bounded poset.

In the example, A_0 is first written as {X | X|o|X}. The correct bottom element of the closure system is {X | X|o|Y ∀Y} (the A_00 of the next page). Grothendieck himself corrects this in the following lines.
Minor: Spat 1 restates that ≤ is an order, which the definition on the previous page already says. The equivalence X|o|Y ⇔ Y ≤ CX uses Spat 2, which is fine.

ideas.what: Axioms Spat1–3: complete lattice with involutive antitone complement satisfying x∧Cx=0
Orthogonality X|o|Y ⇔ X ≤ CY, symmetric and irreflexive on nonzero elements
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality space associated to an ortholattice

ideas.what: From a set with symmetric relation, the biorthogonally closed subsets form a complete lattice with involution, orthocomplemented iff self-orthogonal elements are 'null'
ideas.modern_name: polarity / Galois connection; ortholattice of ⊥-closed subsets of an orthogonality space

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'ateliers spatiaux' are re-derived independently as orthogonality spaces and complete ortholattices, the standard structures of quantum logic. The notes, as visible here, do not mention that literature. This is of biographical and historical interest (his 1986 foundations-of-space programme) but is not new mathematics.
missed.quote: x ∧ Cx = 0_Σ ... X |o| Y ⟺ X ≤ CY ... X|o|X ⟺ X = 0_Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that his late reflections on an axiomatics of space converged on quantum-logic and orthogonality-space structures, with 'interior disjointness' of regions as the base relation. This could interest historians and people working on point-free and mereotopological space.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a correct but standard rediscovery of complete ortholattices and the orthogonality-space ↔ ortholattice correspondence (Birkhoff, Dacey, Foulis–Randall). It is mildly interesting only as Grothendieck's own 1986 route to these structures from a theory of spatial 'ateliers'.
transcription_corrections: The page number at the top is '47' (overwritten); the next page's '98' is likely '48'.

In the example, 'une notion de "recouvrement" de croisement[?]' should more plausibly read 'une notion de "rapport"'. The last line reads roughly 'et un ensemble Σ_A des [rapports] Σ ⊂ P(A)', which continues as 'de rapports, stables dans P(A) par ∩' on the next page.
The parenthetical reads '(A_0 = ∅ dans le cas où A est un ensemble [de parties/régions] et |o| la relation de disjonction intérieure ...)'.
'donc dans Σ* ... la relation |o| est antiréflexive' is preceded by 'Ainsi' on a new line ('Ainsi, en plus d'être symétrique').
